# DevSpark - Technical Summary

**DevSpark** is a structured development process framework designed to integrate AI coding assistants (Claude, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, etc.) into repeatable software engineering workflows without requiring installation. The core product consists of 28 markdown-based slash-command prompts and supporting context-gathering scripts that guide AI agents through the complete development lifecycle—from requirements specification through implementation, code review, and release management.

The architecture employs a dual-surface model separating lifecycle orchestration (via slash-commands in `templates/commands/`) from portable capability packages called "skills" (in `templates/skills/`), with an adapter contract defining how commands invoke skills. Built primarily in Python (52.5%) with supporting PowerShell and Shell scripts, DevSpark leverages a lightweight tech stack (Click, Pydantic, PyYAML, JSONSchema) to provide optional CLI tooling, a harness runtime for declarative workflow execution, and agent registry metadata for multi-platform integration. Three flagship workflow aliases—`create-spec`, `execute-plan`, and `suggest-improvement`—provide opinionated entry points, while the system maintains backward compatibility through the legacy `/devspark.specify` command.

The project exhibits highly active development (261 commits in 90 days, accelerating activity pattern) and prioritizes zero-friction adoption through markdown-first design; users can copy prompts directly into their projects or use the optional CLI for automated setup and environment validation. DevSpark targets teams seeking standardized AI-assisted development processes with governance gates, multi-participant role assignment, and artifact traceability—positioning itself as infrastructure for AI coding workflows rather than a traditional software tool.

# TailwindSpark - Technical Summary

**TailwindSpark** is a production-ready React TypeScript monorepo designed as a comprehensive showcase and learning resource for modern web development with Tailwind CSS 4. | Component | Purpose | Tech Stack |

| **SVG Generator** | Profile statistics visualization | Python + svgwrite |
| **AI Analyzer** | Repository insights & summaries | PyGithub + Claude API |
| **Dashboard** | Interactive web interface | JavaScript/React + Chart.js |
| **GitHub Actions** | Automated weekly updates | YAML workflows |
| **Data Layer** | Caching & persistence | IndexedDB (client-side) |

- **Python (50.0%)**: Core analytics engine and SVG generation
- **JavaScript (20.6%)**: Frontend dashboard and interactivity
- **PowerShell (19.1%)**: Build/deployment automation

- **HTML (1.0%)**: Markup templates

---

**Six Visual Categories:**

| Category | Metric | Algorithm |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Overview Dashboard | Spark Score (0-100) | 40% consistency + 35% volume + 25% collaboration |
| Commit Heatmap | Calendar visualization | GitHub-style contribution intensity mapping |
| Language Statistics | Tech stack breakdown | Repository language composition analysis |
| Streaks & Consistency | Current/longest streaks | Gap-free contribution tracking |
| Fun Stats | 8 personality achievements | Time-of-day patterns, velocity classification |
| Release Cadence | Activity breadth sparklines | Weekly/monthly repository diversity (not raw commits) |

- Automated weekly updates via GitHub Actions (Sundays at 00:00 UTC)
- SVG generation prevents rate-limiting issues vs. dynamic rendering
- WCAG AA accessibility compliance
- Theme customization (dark/light/custom)
- Embeddable as profile README badges

**Intelligent Ranking Algorithm:**
```
Repository Score = 
  (Popularity × 0.30) +    // Stars & forks
  (Activity × 0.45) +      // Recent commits with time-decay
  (Health × 0.25)          // Docs, licensing, maintenance signals
```

- 4-6 sentence technical descriptions
- Purpose, features, technology stack identification
- Architectural pattern recognition
- Uniqueness & use-case highlighting

- Touch-optimized (44×44px minimum targets)
- Bottom sheet navigation (native mobile pattern)
- Swipe gestures for interactions

- Horizontal swiping for navigation

- **Export**: CSV/JSON download of filtered data
- **Offline support**: IndexedDB + Dexie (7-day retention)
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 AA, screen reader support, keyboard navigation

- <2s First Contentful Paint (Lighthouse CI)
- ≥0.9 performance score
- GitHub Pages automated deployment

# API Test Spark - Technical Summary

**API Test Spark** is a .NET 10 NuGet package that embeds an interactive, React-powered API testing harness directly into Minimal API applications with a single line of code (`MapApiTestSpark()`). The package automatically discovers and exposes all OpenAPI v3 endpoints through a feature-rich testing UI accessible at `/api-test-spark/`, eliminating the need for separate testing tools or Swagger UI dependencies.

The solution delivers comprehensive API exploration and documentation capabilities, including OpenAPI autodiscovery with collapsible endpoint grouping, request body scaffolding from schema definitions, Bearer/API key authentication injection, editable nested response fields, copy-as-cURL functionality, JSONPath field tooltips, and a live debug panel for request/response inspection. Advanced features include an integrated API documentation builder for exporting markdown with captured curl commands and responses, support for multiple remote API profiles with independent explorers, environment-aware gating (Development/Staging only), and depth-1 nested object editing with response merging.

The architecture employs a hybrid polyglot approach—the backend is pure C# for .NET 10 Minimal APIs with zero external dependencies, while the frontend is a compiled React SPA (TypeScript/JavaScript) shipped as embedded resources within the NuGet package itself, ensuring no deployment complexity or build process overhead. Configuration follows a fluent builder pattern via `Action<ApiTestSparkOptions>` delegates, supporting customizable OpenAPI URLs, CORS origins, default headers, auth schemes, and remote API profiles.

What distinguishes API Test Spark is its zero-configuration philosophy and embedded-first design: the entire branded React UI compiles into the package (500 KB), eliminating wwwroot modifications and external CDN dependencies, while sensible defaults allow developers to enable full testing capabilities in development/staging environments with a single method call. The project targets .NET 10 developers building Minimal APIs who need production-grade API documentation and testing without Swagger overhead, supported by an active development cadence (137 commits in 90 days) and a live demo running against a real multi-endpoint API.

# BootstrapSpark - Technical Summary

**BootstrapSpark** is a production-ready, enterprise-grade developer portfolio application built with React 19, TypeScript, and Vite, designed to demonstrate modern frontend engineering best practices and cloud-native deployment patterns. The application serves as both a personal portfolio showcase and a comprehensive reference implementation for scalable web development, featuring real-time capabilities through SignalR integration, responsive Bootstrap 5 UI with dark/light theme switching, and multi-platform deployment across Azure Static Web Apps and GitHub Pages with automated CI/CD pipelines via GitHub Actions.

The project showcases advanced technical features including real-time chat with multiple AI personalities, dynamic weather widgets with interactive Leaflet maps, RSS feed integration with XML parsing, searchable project portfolios, and comprehensive accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA). Its architecture employs React Context API for state management, TypeScript with strict mode for type safety, Vite for optimized bundling with code splitting and lazy loading, and integrates external APIs (OpenWeather, JokeAPI) through a serverless Azure Functions proxy layer to manage content security policies.

Key architectural decisions emphasize performance optimization through lazy-loaded components and a frontend-only design pattern that pulls content from external sources, strict type safety with full TypeScript implementation, and developer experience with hot module reloading, ESLint/Prettier formatting, and comprehensive documentation. The tech stack spans 46 dependencies with modern tools including Bootstrap/React-Bootstrap for UI components, date-fns for date utilities, Axios for HTTP communication, and SignalR for real-time bidirectional communication, all configured for production deployment with intentionally permissive CSP headers documented for security transparency.

This repository is ideal for developers seeking a reference implementation of contemporary React patterns, enterprise-grade architecture demonstrations, portfolio creation inspiration, or understanding full-stack cloud deployment strategies with serverless infrastructure. The project's 90+ commits in the last year and consistent activity pattern indicate active maintenance and ongoing refinement, making it a living example of professional web development practices rather than an archived sample project.

**WebSpark.HttpClientUtility** is an enterprise-grade HTTP client wrapper library for .NET 8-10 that dramatically simplifies resilient API consumption through a single-line configuration pattern. # MuseumSpark: Technical Summary

**MuseumSpark** is an intelligent travel planning platform that transforms the Walker Art Center's reciprocal museum membership roster (1,269 North American institutions) into a data-rich, searchable resource for art enthusiasts. Built by Mark Hazleton as a reference architecture, ApiSpark serves as both a functional platform and educational resource for developers seeking scalable yet economical solutions for API consolidation in cloud environments.

# SupportSpark - Technical Summary

**SupportSpark** is a full-stack support network platform built with React 19, Express 5, and TypeScript that enables members to share personal journey updates (health challenges, life transitions) with a trusted circle of supporters through a role-based, invitation-only network. The application features a dual-user model where members create and manage updates while supporters receive real-time notifications, read posts, and engage through threaded conversations—all within a deliberately calm, distraction-free interface designed for sensitive emotional contexts.

The tech stack leverages modern web technologies including Vite for fast development builds, Tailwind CSS 4 for utility-first styling with a soothing teal/sage color palette, Radix UI primitives via shadcn/ui for accessible components (WCAG-compliant), TanStack React Query for server state management, and Zod for runtime type validation. The backend implements session-based authentication via Passport.js with a JSON-file storage layer (development) or database persistence, while the frontend uses Wouter for lightweight client-side routing and Framer Motion for purposeful animations—all with strict TypeScript typing across the stack.

Architecturally, the project demonstrates enterprise patterns including shared type definitions between client and server (via `schema.ts`), separation of concerns across `client/`, `server/`, and `shared/` directories, and comprehensive documentation with a constitution-based governance model. The application supports multiple deployment scenarios: a live production site at `support.makeboldspark.com`, a static GitHub Pages build that runs entirely in the browser using localStorage, and Windows IIS deployment via automated PowerShell scripts with iisnode integration—making it suitable for both cloud and on-premises enterprise environments.

What distinguishes SupportSpark is its intentional design for vulnerable moments: it solves the exhaustion of manually updating multiple contacts by implementing a broadcast-with-threading pattern, emphasizes accessibility and calm UX principles critical for health/life transitions, and provides a demo mode with pre-seeded data for immediate exploration without account creation. The project functions as both a production application and a technical portfolio piece demonstrating full-stack TypeScript competency, role-based access control, real-time collaboration patterns, and deployment expertise across multiple platforms.

summary.text:
# KeyPressCounter - Technical Summary

## Overview
KeyPressCounter is a lightweight Windows system tray utility designed to monitor keyboard and mouse input activity alongside real-time system performance metrics, providing users with comprehensive statistics about their computer usage patterns without recording sensitive data or transmitting information externally. The application runs silently in the background as a single-instance Windows Forms application with a rich dashboard interface for viewing aggregated statistics.

## Key Features & Capabilities
The application combines input monitoring (keystroke and mouse click tracking with peak activity metrics and idle period detection) with comprehensive system performance monitoring, including real-time CPU/memory gauges, disk I/O metrics, network speeds, and a top-10 process monitor. Users benefit from a three-tab statistics dashboard featuring input statistics, system performance graphs (60-second rolling line charts with GDI+ rendering), hardware information via WMI, persistent configuration management, automatic daily summary logging, and quick-launch access to Windows system utilities—all exposed through an intuitive system tray context menu with single-click access to activity logs.

## Technology Stack & Architecture
Built on **.NET 10.0** with **C# 13**, the project leverages **SharpHook** (7.1.1) for global keyboard/mouse event hooking on background threads, **System.Management** for WMI-based hardware enumeration, native Windows Performance Counters for CPU/memory/disk/network metrics, and **User32 P/Invoke** (`GetLastInputInfo`) for idle detection. The architecture follows a modular design pattern with clear separation of concerns: `CustomApplicationContext` manages the tray icon and event lifecycle, `Counter` provides thread-safe increment operations with peak tracking, `SystemPerformanceMonitor` abstracts performance counter management, and `StatsForm` implements the UI dashboard with 1-second refresh intervals.

## Notable Design Patterns & Implementation
The codebase demonstrates strong Windows desktop development practices including thread-safe counter operations with lock-based synchronization, persistent JSON-based configuration stored in `%APPDATA%`, automatic Windows startup registry integration, and comprehensive logging with timestamped activity logs and daily summaries written to the Documents folder. The application enforces single-instance behavior at startup and implements graceful exception handling with global exception handlers to prevent silent failures.

## Unique Aspects & Target Users
KeyPressCounter distinguishes itself through privacy-first design—it counts input events without capturing key identities or recording what users type, making it suitable for productivity tracking, workstation monitoring, or activity analytics in professional environments where privacy compliance is critical. The project targets productivity-conscious users, system administrators tracking workstation utilization, and organizations needing lightweight activity baselines without intrusive keystroke logging.

## Current Project Status
The repository shows signs of maturity but inactivity: zero commits in 365 days, no recent activity, and a tech stack currency score of 57/100, indicating the project may require updates to remain compatible with current .NET versions and security best practices, though the core functionality remains sound for Windows 10+ environments.

# Technical Summary: WebProjectMechanics

**WebProjectMechanics** is a greenfield rebuild of a legacy multi-tenant content management system designed to serve 36+ independent websites from a single application instance while maintaining physical data isolation and minimal infrastructure costs (~$10/month). The system architecture employs a plugin-based domain model with domain-specific content types (CMS pages, mineral collections, recipes), per-site SQLite databases for tenant isolation, and a publish-to-static workflow that pre-renders all public content as HTML served by Caddy, eliminating database queries in the critical path. Built on ASP.NET Core 9 with EF Core 9, the project leverages modern .NET patterns including Minimal APIs, dependency injection, and xUnit testing while using Scriban for templating and GitHub Actions for CI/CD on Ubuntu 24.04. The codebase is structured around separation of concerns with shared contracts (WPM.Core), infrastructure services, a minimal API host, and isolated domain projects, complemented by comprehensive documentation of both the legacy system it's replacing and the phased implementation plan. This approach is particularly noteworthy for its cost-efficiency, data isolation without tenant IDs, and the pragmatic decision to maintain a read-only archive of the 20+ year legacy system, making it an excellent case study in migrating complex enterprise applications to modern cloud-native architectures while preserving operational continuity.

# Technical Summary: WebSpark.PrismSpark

**WebSpark.PrismSpark** is a modern C#/.NET 10 port of the popular PrismJS syntax highlighting library, providing advanced code highlighting, theming, and extensibility capabilities for .NET web applications. The project delivers tokenization and syntax highlighting for 24 programming languages (C#, JavaScript, Python, Markdown, Pug, etc.) with a robust plugin system supporting line numbers, copy-to-clipboard, toolbars, and custom extensions, alongside a comprehensive theme system with built-in themes and CSS generation capabilities.

The architecture employs a modular design pattern with clear separation of concerns—featuring core tokenization engines, language-specific grammars, plugin and hook systems for extensibility, and specialized highlighter implementations (HtmlHighlighter, EnhancedHtmlHighlighter, ThemedHtmlHighlighter) that support advanced options like line highlighting, custom CSS classes, async processing, and caching. The codebase is primarily C# (72.9%) with supporting HTML, PowerShell, JavaScript, and CSS components, and includes a comprehensive test suite of 52 MSTest tests covering grammar validation, tokenization, highlighting workflows, and integration scenarios.

The project stands out through its tight ASP.NET Core MVC integration via dependency injection, live interactive demo pages (including a real-time code editor and markdown processor), and production-ready performance considerations with async/caching APIs—making it particularly valuable for developers building documentation sites, code review platforms, learning management systems, and technical blogging platforms within the .NET ecosystem. However, the repository shows signs of being inactive (zero commits in 90-365 days, no contributors or stars recorded), suggesting it may be a completed demonstration project or archived reference implementation rather than an actively maintained production library.
